title: Cancel a long job
description:
Let a slow job be cancelled and report progress.

```
progress 10%
progress 20%
progress 30%
cancelled at 30%
```
hints: Pass the token to `Task.Delay(50, token)`: it throws as soon as the token is cancelled (lesson 5.02).
`Progress<T>` may run its callback slightly later; a plain class implementing `IProgress<int>` reports straight away if the order matters.
requirements: `async Task Work(IProgress<int> progress, CancellationToken token)` does 10 steps of 50 ms, reporting after each.
Catch `OperationCanceledException` and print where it stopped.
stretch: Let the user press Enter to cancel instead of a timer.
